newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vereinsbank sees 97 profit up over 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank sees 97 profit up over 10 pct.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG said on Wednesday it was aiming for a double-digit percentage rise in operating profit after risk provisions in 1997.
Germany's fourth-largest listed bank said in a statement that operating profit before risk provisions rose 18.7 percent to 614.7 million marks ($356.6 million) in the first quarter of 1997.

Earnings in the period were buoyed by a 96.6 percent jump in own-account trading profit to 98.0 million marks. New mortgage lending remained at the high level reached in the year-earlier period, Vereinsbank said. ($ = 1.723 German Marks)
Vereinsbank chief executive Albrecht Schmidt said he was "very pleased" with business in the first three months.
"We're above plan and want to continue the momentum of the first quarter. We have set a goal of achieving a double-digit (percentage) rise in operating profit after risk provisions for 1997 as well."
In 1996, Vereinsbank increased its operating profit after risk provisions by 18.4 percent to 1.636 billion marks.
The statement was released ahead of Vereinsbank's annual shareholder meeting today.
Net interest income in the first quarter rose by 5.3 percent to 1.2 billion marks while net commission income was up 17.4 percent at 351.7 million marks, the bank said.

Vereinsbank also said it almost matched the extraordinarily strong new mortgage business seen in the first quarter of 1996, with new loan approvals in the first three months of 1997 reaching 12.7 billion marks, down just 3.1 percent year-on-year.
The group lending volume rose by 1.6 percent to 317.4 billion marks, while the group balance sheet total rose by 1.5 percent to 409.6 billion marks.
